rules.statement: The failure to object to a document marked subject to proof when the case is closed constitutes waiver of the objection.
rules.supporting_quote: Per Edussuriya, J. �(1) Deed P11 though marked subject to proof was not objected to when the respondents case was closed reading in evidence P1-P17. "Where no objection is taken when a document is read in evidence at the closure of the case to a document which had been marked subject to proof the earlier objection is deemed to have been waived." In any event, the Notary gave evidence and had stated that she knew the Donor, Donee and the two attesting witnesses. (2) The defendants-appellants are not bona fide possessors; trespassers cannot foist on the owner what they consider to be necessary improvements done without the owners consent and claim compensation. Per Senanayake, J. (3) "It is well settled law that a male fide possessor was not entitled under the Roman Dutch Law to compensation for Impensa Utiles, except in cases where the owner of the property stood by and allowed the building to proceed without 268 notice to his own claim, in such a case the male fide possessor would be in the position of a bona fide possessor with the rights of retention." (4) The appellants cannot under any circumstances according to law claim any compensation on the basis of unjust enrichment. It would be unreasonable to allow him to force on the true owner improvements which may be useful according to his own taste, which the plaintiff-respondent never cared to effect
